Boohoo Group Sticks to Guidance After Earnings Improve
Boohoo Group maintained its guidance amid a continuing turnaround after the fashion group returned to growth with improved earnings in the first half of its fiscal year.

The company, which trades as Debenhams, said Thursday that earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization for the six months ended Aug. 31 were 20 million pounds ($26.8 million) compared to a loss of 3 million pounds for the same period a year earlier.
Adjusted Ebitda rose 14% to 24 million pounds.
Gross merchandise value before returns rose to 864 million pounds from 849 million pounds, while the gross margin was 53.9% compared with 51.9%.
"The return to growth has been supported by a record marketplace mix, materially improved profitability and significantly improved cash flows," the company said.

As part of its fiscal 2027 guidance, Boohoo expects to deliver GMV growth as well as double-digit adjusted Ebitda growth in line with consensus of no less than 59 million pounds, it said. The company expects continued material improvement in Ebitda, with a return to profit before tax and free cash flow generation.
Boohoo's turnaround progresses at pace, Chief Executive Officer Dan Finley said.

"Since the half year end, the Sheffield distribution centre and Nasty Gal disposals mark a further significant step in reducing leverage, and we now expect net debt to be negligible at our February 2027 year end."
